evidence: PwC issued unqualified opinions on the 2025 financial statements and internal control over financial reporting.
No filing reviewed indicates a material accounting restatement or management-integrity impairment.
Cash plus investments were ~$8.63B at 2026-06-30 versus total liabilities of ~$2.58B.
H1 2026 operating cash flow was $1.97B and management expects growth investments to be funded from operations.
Shares outstanding declined from 355.1M at 2025-12-31 to 353.9M at 2026-06-30 as repurchases more than offset issuance.
SBC remains material and must continue to be monitored.
Growth is driven by procedure volume, installed-base expansion, consumables, service and utilization rather than subsidies or uneconomic marketing.
Recurring revenue was 85% of H1 2026 revenue.
Revenue, operating income and operating cash flow continue to grow while gross margins remain high.
No evidence in the reviewed filings indicates structural collapse in reinvestment returns; however leasing and manufacturing investments increase capital intensity.
Global procedure growth, installed-base growth and recurring revenue indicate the ecosystem remains strong.
China is a localized moat-pressure signal but has not yet translated into persistent global competitive contraction.

At $369.83, reverse DCF requires roughly 11%-13% annual FCF growth for ten years depending on terminal multiple assumptions; demanding, but not an unrealistic bull-case-only outcome given current procedure and revenue growth.
The lack of a large expectation gap is reflected in a low valuation score rather than a veto.

da Vinci is the dominant economic platform, but revenue is diversified across thousands of hospital customers, multiple procedures, geographies, consumables, service and leases; Ion/SP add adjacencies.
Dependence on the robotic-surgery ecosystem remains a material strategic concentration but not currently fatal.
Large net cash resources, no conventional funded debt burden, positive FCF and recurring revenue make bankruptcy risk remote under normal stress scenarios.
Primary permanent-loss mechanism is competitive/regulatory erosion plus valuation compression, not solvency.
